findings.english_quote: The makers appear to be two
findings.issue: The draft renders the preceding πλάσαντός as “fashioned” but changes the repeated verb here to generic “makers.” This obscures the shared wording connecting Simon's two assertions and its distinction from ποιήσωμεν, rendered “make” in the quotation. No contextual exception is documented.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “Those who fashioned you appear to be two,” with a note, if needed, explaining that “you” is understood from the preceding clause. This proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.issue: The contextual choice “tempter” is defensible, but the note incorrectly says that the repeated testing root is retained in English: “tempter” and “testing” use different roots. It also calls the Greek expression a noun, although πειράζων is a substantivized participle. The more neutral, root-transparent alternative is not expressly preserved.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the main wording with “the one who tests was testing” or “the tester was testing.” If retaining “the tempter was testing,” revise the note to acknowledge the English lexical variation, identify the participial construction correctly, preserve the neutral alternative, and explain that the preceding temptation to apostasy and Peter's argument against divine testing support the chosen rendering. This uncertainty does not require a source-verification block.

findings.issue: The supplied image-checked reading contains a middle dot immediately before γραφῶν. The draft leaves this apparent typographical or editorial feature unreported. Its unusual position should not be silently attributed to OCR or treated as evidence of missing words.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted source_issues entry recording the prefixed point and explaining that the English translates the surviving wording without assigning lexical content to the point. Distinguish this print feature from an unresolved corruption or an established lacuna; do not invent a restoration.

findings.issue: The additive καὶ is not represented. Unlike a merely transitional conjunction, its position here adds the Messiah's sonship to the preceding description of the creator.
findings.suggested_revision: Render “whose son the Messiah also is.” Do not explain “also” as establishing other sons, which this wording does not itself specify.

findings.source_quote: ᾧ πειθόμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν τὰ ψευδῆ ἐπιγινώσκομεν
findings.english_quote: In obedience to him, we recognize the false things in the scriptures.
findings.issue: The main rendering takes ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν as locating or sourcing the false material within scripture. That is contextually defensible, especially beside the following reference to scripture's true material. However, the phrase can also attach to the act of recognition: scripture supplies the evidence by which falsehood is recognized. This materially different attachment is not disclosed; the existing note addresses only the antecedent of “him.”
findings.suggested_revision: The main wording may remain, but add a source-quoted note preserving the alternative “In obedience to him, we recognize what is false from the scriptures,” understood as recognition on scriptural evidence. Explain why the contrast with the following true scriptural material favors the chosen reading. Do not present either attachment as uniquely established.

findings.source_quote: τοῦτον καὶ θεοφιλεῖ λογισμῷ ἀληθὲς ὂν δογματίσαντες οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν
findings.english_quote: The fathers, declaring this to be true by reasoning that loves God, handed him down to us
findings.issue: The English distinguishes propositional “this” from personal “him,” but the note does not explain that interpretive treatment of masculine τοῦτον alongside neuter ἀληθὲς ὂν. A contextual understanding referring to the truth of the preceding assertion is defensible. Another viable analysis takes ὂν substantivally, yielding an affirmation of this God as “a true being.” The existing note discusses θεοφιλεῖ but leaves this separate construction unexplained.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note stating that the main rendering understands the neuter phrase as characterizing the assertion about the one creator. Preserve the alternative “having affirmed this one as a true being through God-loving reasoning, the fathers handed him on to us.” Retain the supplied Greek without alleging OCR corruption or silently changing its gender. Any replacement main text requires fresh review.

findings.issue: The supplied reading has a point immediately before δὲ. As with the prefixed point in 16.13, this apparent print feature is not disclosed. The surviving words are translated, so this is not itself evidence of omitted content or an unreadable construction.
findings.suggested_revision: Record “ἔτι .δὲ” in source_issues as an apparent typographical or editorial feature. Explain that no letters have been corrected and no missing wording restored; do not label the independently image-checked point an OCR error or an established lacuna without evidence.
